groups.context: A community center lobby has a long reception desk. A staff member is handing a visitor a printed badge while two people wait near a notice board.
Outside a public library, two workers are placing books into labeled plastic crates beside a small delivery van.
In a multipurpose hall, a technician is adjusting a ceiling-mounted projector while rows of empty chairs face a screen.
At a neighborhood garden, three volunteers are filling watering cans from an outdoor tap beside raised planting beds.
Inside a bicycle workshop, a mechanic is tightening a bolt on a bicycle wheel while helmets hang from hooks on the wall.
At an outdoor information booth, a woman is attaching a schedule poster to a display board while another worker holds a roll of tape.

M: The repair café is busier than expected. We have five people waiting for appliance checks.

N: Attention, community shuttle passengers. Because Pine Street is closed for utility work, the 9:20 shuttle will skip the Pine Street stop and use Oak Avenue instead. Passengers for the health clinic should get off at Oak Avenue and walk one block east. The regular route is expected to resume after noon.

N: This is a reminder for tonight’s community cooking class. The class will begin at six in Kitchen B, not Kitchen A. Please bring a reusable container if you want to take food home. Aprons and basic utensils are provided. Participants should check in at the front desk before going downstairs.

N: Vendors at Saturday’s neighborhood market should note a change to unloading. Vehicles may enter the service lane from 6:30 to 7:15 a.m. After 7:15, the lane becomes pedestrian-only. Vendors arriving later must use the public parking lot and carry goods through the south gate. Market staff will provide carts near that gate.

N: Welcome to the shared woodworking workshop. Before using any power tool, complete the short safety demonstration at the red bench. Eye protection is stored in the cabinet beside the bench. If a tool develops a problem, switch it off and attach a yellow tag. Do not attempt repairs yourself. A technician checks tagged equipment every afternoon.

N: The neighborhood recycling event begins at nine on Sunday in the civic center parking lot. Paper, metal cans, and small electronics are accepted. Glass will not be collected this month because the processing truck is unavailable. Volunteers can help unload items, but residents should remove personal data from electronic devices before arriving.
